q = QuantumRegister(3, 'q')
c = ClassicalRegister(3, 'c')
teleportation_circuit = QuantumCircuit(q, c)

# Stage 1: Initialize the state to be teleported on q0
# We want to teleport |1>, so we apply an X gate.
teleportation_circuit.x(q[0])
teleportation_circuit.barrier()

# Stage 2: Create an entangled Bell pair between q1 and q2
teleportation_circuit.h(q[1])
teleportation_circuit.cx(q[1], q[2])
teleportation_circuit.barrier()

# Stage 3: Alice's operations on her qubits (q0 and q1)
teleportation_circuit.cx(q[0], q[1])
teleportation_circuit.h(q[0])
teleportation_circuit.barrier()

# Stage 4: Alice measures her qubits and sends the classical results to Bob
teleportation_circuit.measure(q[0], c[0])
teleportation_circuit.measure(q[1], c[1])
teleportation_circuit.barrier()

# Stage 5: Bob applies gates to his qubit (q2) based on the classical bits
# In a real quantum computer, these would be classically controlled operations.
# qc.x(q[2]).c_if(c[1], 1)
# qc.z(q[2]).c_if(c[0], 1)
# The prompt asks for the standard textbook representation using quantum-controlled gates.
teleportation_circuit.cx(q[1], q[2])
teleportation_circuit.cz(q[0], q[2])
teleportation_circuit.barrier()

# Stage 6: Bob measures his qubit to confirm the teleported state
teleportation_circuit.measure(q[2], c[2])

```python
# Define the quantum and classical registers
q_inputs = QuantumRegister(4, 'q')
q_ancilla = QuantumRegister(1, 'ancilla')
c_outputs = ClassicalRegister(4, 'c')

# Create the quantum circuit
dj_circuit = QuantumCircuit(q_inputs, q_ancilla, c_outputs)

# 1. Prepare the ancilla in the |1> state
dj_circuit.x(q_ancilla[0])

# 2. Apply Hadamard gates to all qubits
dj_circuit.h(q_inputs)
dj_circuit.h(q_ancilla)

dj_circuit.barrier()

# 3. Implement the balanced oracle
# This oracle implements f(x) = x_3 (the fourth input bit)
# It's balanced because f(x)=1 for half the inputs and f(x)=0 for the other half.
dj_circuit.cnot(q_inputs[3], q_ancilla[0])

dj_circuit.barrier()

# 4. Apply Hadamard gates to the input qubits
dj_circuit.h(q_inputs)

# 5. Measure the input qubits
dj_circuit.measure(q_inputs, c_outputs)
```

```python
# The inverse of CX(0,2) is CX(0,2)
```

q_in = QuantumRegister(2, 'input')
q_out = QuantumRegister(2, 'output')
c_out = ClassicalRegister(2, 'result')
half_adder = QuantumCircuit(q_in, q_out, c_out, name="Half Adder")

# Initialize input bits to 1
half_adder.x(q_in[0])
half_adder.x(q_in[1])
half_adder.barrier()

# Compute sum (a XOR b)
# The sum is stored in output qubit 0
half_adder.cx(q_in[0], q_out[0])
half_adder.cx(q_in[1], q_out[0])
half_adder.barrier()

# Compute carry (a AND b)
# The carry is stored in output qubit 1
half_adder.ccx(q_in[0], q_in[1], q_out[1])
half_adder.barrier()

# Measure the output qubits
# c_out[0] will be the sum, c_out[1] will be the carry
half_adder.measure(q_out[0], c_out[0])
half_adder.measure(q_out[1], c_out[1])
